original_text:
Mitosis -Anaphase
Chromatids of each chromosome separate at the centromere 
Slowly move, centromere first, toward opposite poles of cell 
After chromatids separate 
considered to be individual chromosomes
explanation: Anaphase is characterized by the separation of the sister chromatids of each chromosome. They split at the centromere and are pulled slowly toward opposite poles of the cell, moving centromere-first. Once chromatids separate, they are considered to be individual chromosomes.

questions.q: What key event defines anaphase in mitosis?
opts: Chromosomes align at the metaphase plate.
Chromatids of each chromosome separate at the centromere and move toward opposite poles.
The nuclear envelope reforms around chromosomes.
DNA wraps around histones to form chromatin.
questions.exp: Anaphase begins when chromatids of each chromosome separate at the centromere and slowly move toward opposite poles of the cell.
